summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image based on Ubuntu that installs Firefox from Mozilla's official APT repository. It sets up the necessary repository keys and configurations, then installs Firefox as the default command to run when the container starts.

explanations.1: This comment tells spell-checkers to ignore this file, since Docker syntax might contain words they don't recognize.
explanations.5: This environment variable tells the system to run in non-interactive mode, so it won't prompt for user input during installation.
explanations.7: The double ampersand (&&) chains commands together — if one fails, the rest won't run — and the backslash at the end continues the command on the next line for readability.
explanations.9: This removes the cached package lists after installation to make the Docker image smaller, since we won't need them again.
explanations.12: The --mount directives create temporary storage areas during this build step: the first two cache package data so reinstalls are faster, and the third redirects logs to RAM so they don't bloat the image.
explanations.16: The 'install -d' command creates directories if they don't exist; '-m 0755' sets permissions; this prepares the system to accept the Mozilla repository key.
explanations.18: This downloads Mozilla's signing key and pipes it to gpg, which decodes it (dearmor) and saves it to a file that APT will use to verify Firefox packages are legitimate.
explanations.21: This echo command creates the actual repository configuration line and pipes it to 'tee', which writes it to a file while also suppressing output.
explanations.24: This sets APT to prefer Firefox packages from Mozilla's repository (priority 1000 is very high) rather than from Ubuntu's default repositories.
explanations.26: The '-qq' flag makes apt-get extra quiet (only show errors), and '> /dev/null' discards any output, keeping the build logs clean.
explanations.30: This sets Firefox as the default command — when someone runs this Docker image, it will automatically launch Firefox.
